sanskrit: atha saṃvatsare pūrṇe tasmin prāpte turaṅgame sarayvāś cottare tīre rājño yajño 'bhyavartata
english: Then, when a full year had passed and the horse had returned, the king's sacrifice commenced on the northern bank of the Sarayū.

sanskrit: ṛśyaśṛṅgaṃ puraskṛtya karma cakrur dvijarṣabhāḥ aśvamedhe mahāyajñe rājño 'sya sumahātmanaḥ
english: With Ṛśyaśṛṅga placed at their head, the foremost of the twice-born performed the rites of the great Aśvamedha sacrifice for this most noble king.

sanskrit: karma kurvanti vidhivad yājakā vedapāragāḥ yathāvidhi yathānyāyaṃ parikrāmanti śāstrataḥ
english: The officiating priests, masters of the Veda, performed the rites according to injunction, proceeding in proper order and in strict accordance with the śāstras.

sanskrit: pravargyaṃ śāstrataḥ kṛtvā tathaivopasadaṃ dvijāḥ cakruś ca vidhivat sarvam adhikaṃ karma śāstrataḥ
english: The twice-born performed the pravargya rite according to the śāstra, and likewise the upasad ceremony; they carried out every additional rite in conformity with rule and scripture.

sanskrit: abhipūjya tato hṛṣṭāḥ sarve cakrur yathāvidhi prātaḥsavanapūrvāṇi karmāṇi munipuṃgavāḥ
english: Then, paying due honour and filled with joy, all those foremost of sages duly performed the rites beginning with the morning pressing of Soma.

sanskrit: na cāhutam abhūt tatra skhalitaṃ vāpi kiṃ cana dṛśyate brahmavat sarvaṃ kṣemayuktaṃ hi cakrire
english: There was nothing left unoblated, nor was any lapse at all observed; everything was done as befitting Brahman itself, carried out with full auspiciousness.

sanskrit: na teṣv ahaḥsu śrānto vā kṣudhito vāpi dṛśyate nāvidvān brāhmaṇas tatra nāśatānucaras tathā
english: On those days none was seen to be weary or hungry; no brāhmaṇa there was unlearned, and none had fewer than a hundred attendants.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇā bhuñjate nityaṃ nāthavantaś ca bhuñjate tāpasā bhuñjate cāpi śramaṇā bhuñjate tathā
english: Brāhmaṇas ate freely, the protected and dependent also ate; ascetics ate, and wandering mendicants ate as well.

sanskrit: vṛddhāś ca vyādhitāś caiva striyo bālās tathaiva ca aniśaṃ bhuñjamānānāṃ na tṛptir upalabhyate
english: The aged and the infirm, women and children likewise — though eating without interruption, no satiation was perceived among them.

sanskrit: dīyatāṃ dīyatām annaṃ vāsāṃsi vividhāni ca iti saṃcoditās tatra tathā cakrur anekaśaḥ
english: 'Give, give food! Give garments of every kind!' — thus urged, the attendants did so again and again, many times over.

sanskrit: annakūṭāś ca bahavo dṛśyante parvatopamāḥ divase divase tatra siddhasya vidhivat tadā
english: And many heaps of cooked food, resembling mountains, were seen there each day, prepared properly and in abundance.

sanskrit: annaṃ hi vidhivat svādu praśaṃsanti dvijarṣabhāḥ aho tṛptāḥ sma bhadraṃ te iti śuśrāva rāghavaḥ
english: The foremost of the twice-born praised the food — duly prepared and delicious — saying 'Ah, we are satisfied! Blessings upon you!' — and Rāghava heard this.

sanskrit: svalaṃkṛtāś ca puruṣā brāhmaṇān paryaveṣayan upāsate ca tān anye sumṛṣṭamaṇikuṇḍalāḥ
english: Well-adorned men served the brāhmaṇas, while others, wearing polished jewelled earrings, waited upon them with reverence.

sanskrit: karmāntare tadā viprā hetuvādān bahūn api prāhuḥ suvāgmino dhīrāḥ parasparajigīṣayā
english: In the intervals between rites, eloquent and steadfast brāhmaṇas propounded many reasoned arguments, each desiring to surpass the others.

sanskrit: divase divase tatra saṃstare kuśalā dvijāḥ sarvakarmāṇi cakrus te yathāśāstraṃ pracoditāḥ
english: Day by day there, upon the sacrificial ground, skilled twice-born men performed all the rites as enjoined by the śāstras.

sanskrit: nāṣaḍaṅgavid atrāsīn nāvrato nābahuśrutaḥ sadasyas tasya vai rājño nāvādakuśalo dvijaḥ
english: No member of that king's sacrificial assembly was ignorant of the six Vedic auxiliaries, nor one lacking vows, nor unlearned in sacred lore, nor a brāhmaṇa unskilled in disputation.

sanskrit: prāpte yūpocchraye tasmin ṣaḍ bailvāḥ khādirās tathā tāvanto bilvasahitāḥ parṇinaś ca tathāpare
english: When the erection of the sacrificial posts arrived, six posts of bilva wood and as many of khadira were set up, together with those of bilva combined, and others made of paṇin wood.

sanskrit: śleṣmātakamayo diṣṭo devadārumayas tathā dvāv eva tatra vihitau bāhuvyastaparigrahau
english: One post was ordained to be of śleṣmātaka wood and one of devadāru; two posts were appointed there whose circumference was as a man's outstretched arms.

sanskrit: kāritāḥ sarva evaite śāstrajñair yajñakovidaiḥ śobhārthaṃ tasya yajñasya kāñcanālaṃkṛtā bhavan
english: All these were fashioned by those versed in scripture and skilled in sacrifice; for the glory of that sacrifice they were adorned with gold.

sanskrit: vinyastā vidhivat sarve śilpibhiḥ sukṛtā dṛḍhāḥ aṣṭāśrayaḥ sarva eva ślakṣṇarūpasamanvitāḥ
english: All were duly set in place by craftsmen, well made and firm, each with eight facets, all polished and comely in appearance.

sanskrit: ācchāditās te vāsobhiḥ puṣpair gandhaiś ca bhūṣitāḥ saptarṣayo dīptimanto virājante yathā divi
english: Draped with garments and adorned with flowers and fragrant substances, they shone resplendently like the seven brilliant ṛṣis in heaven.

sanskrit: iṣṭakāś ca yathānyāyaṃ kāritāś ca pramāṇataḥ cito 'gnir brāhmaṇais tatra kuśalaiḥ śulbakarmaṇi
english: Bricks were also made in proper measure and proportion; there the sacrificial fire altar was built by brāhmaṇas skilled in the science of the cord.

sanskrit: sa cityo rājasiṃhasya saṃcitaḥ kuśalair dvijaiḥ garuḍo rukmapakṣo vai triguṇo 'ṣṭādaśātmakaḥ
english: That fire altar of the lion among kings, built by skilled twice-born men, was in the form of Garuḍa with golden wings, triple in extent and eighteen-layered.

sanskrit: niyuktās tatra paśavas tat tad uddiśya daivatam uragāḥ pakṣiṇaś caiva yathāśāstraṃ pracoditāḥ śāmitre tu hayas tatra tathā jala carāś ca ye
english: The sacrificial animals were assigned there to their respective deities — serpents and birds as well, all as enjoined by scripture; and at the śāmitra post stood the horse and also the aquatic creatures.

sanskrit: ṛtvigbhiḥ sarvam evaitan niyuktaṃ śāstratas tadā paśūnāṃ triśataṃ tatra yūpeṣu niyataṃ tadā aśvaratnottamaṃ tasya rājño daśarathasya ha
english: All of this was assigned by the officiating priests in accordance with scripture; three hundred sacrificial animals were bound to the posts at that time, along with the chief jewel of horses belonging to king Daśaratha.

sanskrit: kausalyā taṃ hayaṃ tatra paricarya samantataḥ kṛpāṇair viśaśāsainaṃ tribhiḥ paramayā mudā
english: Kausalyā, having reverently attended upon that horse from all sides, slew it with three knives with supreme joy.

sanskrit: patatriṇā tadā sārdhaṃ susthitena ca cetasā avasad rajanīm ekāṃ kausalyā dharmakāmyayā
english: Then Kausalyā passed one night beside that winged creature, her mind composed and steadfast, out of her desire to fulfil dharma.

sanskrit: hotādhvaryus tathodgātā hayena samayojayan mahiṣyā parivṛktyātha vāvātām aparāṃ tathā
english: The hotṛ, the adhvaryu, and the udgātṛ then ceremonially united the horse with the mahiṣī, the parivṛktī, and the vāvātā in turn.

sanskrit: patatriṇas tasya vapām uddhṛtya niyatendriyaḥ ṛtvik parama saṃpannaḥ śrapayām āsa śāstrataḥ
english: An officiating priest of the highest excellence, with his senses fully controlled, drew out the caul-fat of the winged creature and cooked it according to scriptural rite.

sanskrit: dhūmagandhaṃ vapāyās tu jighrati sma narādhipaḥ yathākālaṃ yathānyāyaṃ nirṇudan pāpam ātmanaḥ
english: The lord of men then inhaled the fragrant smoke of that caul-fat at the proper time and in the proper manner, thereby expelling the sin from his own self.

sanskrit: hayasya yāni cāṅgāni tāni sarvāṇi brāhmaṇāḥ agnau prāsyanti vidhivat samastāḥ ṣoḍaśartvijaḥ
english: All the limbs of the horse — every one — the brāhmaṇas cast into the fire in due order; all sixteen of the officiating priests together did so according to rule.

sanskrit: plakṣaśākhāsu yajñānām anyeṣāṃ kriyate haviḥ aśvamedhasya caikasya vaitaso bhāga iṣyate
english: In other sacrifices the oblation is offered on branches of the plakṣa tree, but in the Aśvamedha alone the portion offered in the vaitasa manner is prescribed.

sanskrit: tryaho 'śvamedhaḥ saṃkhyātaḥ kalpasūtreṇa brāhmaṇaiḥ catuṣṭomam ahas tasya prathamaṃ parikalpitam
english: The Aśvamedha is reckoned to last three days according to the Kalpasūtra of the brāhmaṇas; the first day of it is appointed as the Catuṣṭoma day.

sanskrit: ukthyaṃ dvitīyaṃ saṃkhyātam atirātraṃ tathottaram kāritās tatra bahavo vihitāḥ śāstradarśanāt
english: The second is reckoned as the Ukthya, and the following night as the Atirātra; many additional rites were performed there as ordained by the śāstra.

sanskrit: jyotiṣṭomāyuṣī caiva atirātrau ca nirmitau abhijid viśvajic caiva aptoryāmo mahākratuḥ
english: The Jyotiṣṭoma and Āyuṣī and the two Atirātra rites were also performed, as were the Abhijit, the Viśvajit, and the great rite Āptoryāma.

sanskrit: prācīṃ hotre dadau rājā diśaṃ svakulavardhanaḥ adhvaryave pratīcīṃ tu brahmaṇe dakṣiṇāṃ diśam
english: The king, increaser of his lineage, gave the eastern quarter to the hotṛ as his sacrificial fee, the western quarter to the adhvaryu, and the southern quarter to the brahman priest.

sanskrit: udgātre tu tathodīcīṃ dakṣiṇaiṣā vinirmitā aśvamedhe mahāyajñe svayambhuvihite purā
english: And the northern quarter was given to the udgātṛ — this is the southern (dakṣiṇā) prescribed of old by Svayambhū (the Self-born, Brahmā) for the great Aśvamedha sacrifice.

sanskrit: kratuṃ samāpya tu tadā nyāyataḥ puruṣarṣabhaḥ ṛtvigbhyo hi dadau rājā dharāṃ tāṃ kratuvardhanaḥ
english: Having completed the sacrifice with due ceremony, that bull among men, the king who had magnified the rite, then gave the earth itself to the officiating priests.

sanskrit: ṛtvijas tv abruvan sarve rājānaṃ gatakalmaṣam bhavān eva mahīṃ kṛtsnām eko rakṣitum arhati
english: All the officiating priests then addressed the king, now freed of sin: 'You alone are worthy to protect the entire earth.'

sanskrit: na bhūmyā kāryam asmākaṃ na hi śaktāḥ sma pālane ratāḥ svādhyāyakaraṇe vayaṃ nityaṃ hi bhūmipa niṣkrayaṃ kiṃ cid eveha prayacchatu bhavān iti
english: 'We have no use for land; we are not capable of governing it. We are always devoted to the study of the Veda, O lord of the earth — let Your Majesty give us some other ransom in its place.'

sanskrit: gavāṃ śatasahasrāṇi daśa tebhyo dadau nṛpaḥ daśakoṭiṃ suvarṇasya rajatasya caturguṇam
english: The king then gave them ten hundred thousand cows, ten crores' worth of gold, and silver four times that amount.

sanskrit: ṛtvijas tu tataḥ sarve pradaduḥ sahitā vasu ṛśyaśṛṅgāya munaye vasiṣṭhāya ca dhīmate
english: Then all the officiating priests together presented that wealth to the sage Ṛśyaśṛṅga and to the wise Vasiṣṭha.

sanskrit: tatas te nyāyataḥ kṛtvā pravibhāgaṃ dvijottamāḥ suprītamanasaḥ sarve pratyūcur muditā bhṛśam
english: Then those foremost of twice-born men, having made a lawful distribution of it, all spoke in reply with minds exceedingly well pleased and filled with delight.

sanskrit: tataḥ prītamanā rājā prāpya yajñam anuttamam pāpāpahaṃ svarnayanaṃ dustaraṃ pārthivarṣabhaiḥ
english: Then the king, with a gladdened heart, having accomplished that unsurpassed sacrifice — which dispels sin, leads to the heavenly path, and is difficult of attainment even for the foremost of kings —

sanskrit: tato 'bravīd ṛśyaśṛṅgaṃ rājā daśarathas tadā kulasya vardhanaṃ tat tu kartum arhasi suvrata
english: — then said to Ṛśyaśṛṅga, king Daśaratha spoke thus: 'O one of excellent vows, it is fitting that you accomplish the perpetuation of my lineage.'

sanskrit: tatheti ca sa rājānam uvāca dvijasattamaḥ bhaviṣyanti sutā rājaṃś catvāras te kulodvahāḥ
english: 'So be it,' that foremost of twice-born men replied to the king: 'O king, four sons will be born to you, bearers of your lineage.'

sanskrit: medhāvī tu tato dhyātvā sa kiṃ cid idam uttamam labdhasaṃjñas tatas taṃ tu vedajño nṛpam abravīt
english: That wise one then meditated for a moment on something excellent; having collected himself, the knower of the Vedas then addressed the king.

sanskrit: iṣṭiṃ te 'haṃ kariṣyāmi putrīyāṃ putrakāraṇāt atharvaśirasi proktair mantraiḥ siddhāṃ vidhānataḥ
english: 'I shall perform for you the putrīyā iṣṭi — the sacrifice for the sake of sons — accomplished with the mantras proclaimed in the Atharvaśiras, in accordance with the prescribed procedure.'

sanskrit: tataḥ prākramad iṣṭiṃ tāṃ putrīyāṃ putra kāraṇāt juhāva cāgnau tejasvī mantradṛṣṭena karmaṇā
english: Then he commenced that putrīyā iṣṭi for the sake of sons; the brilliant sage poured oblations into the fire by the ritual action prescribed in the mantras.

sanskrit: tato devāḥ sagandharvāḥ siddhāś ca paramarṣayaḥ bhāgapratigrahārthaṃ vai samavetā yathāvidhi
english: Then the gods, together with the gandharvas, the siddhas, and the great ṛṣis assembled in due order for the reception of their shares.

sanskrit: tāḥ sametya yathānyāyaṃ tasmin sadasi devatāḥ abruvaṃl lokakartāraṃ brahmāṇaṃ vacanaṃ mahat
english: Those deities, having duly assembled in that sacrificial hall, addressed a great speech to Brahmā, the maker of worlds.

sanskrit: bhagavaṃs tvatprasādena rāvaṇo nāma rākṣasaḥ sarvānno bādhate vīryāc chāsituṃ taṃ na śaknumaḥ
english: 'O blessed one, through your favour a rākṣasa named Rāvaṇa oppresses us all with his might; we are unable to restrain him.'

sanskrit: tvayā tasmai varo dattaḥ prītena bhagavan purā mānayantaś ca taṃ nityaṃ sarvaṃ tasya kṣamāmahe
english: 'A boon was granted to him by you in times past, O blessed one, out of your pleasure; and out of constant respect for that, we endure everything from him.'

sanskrit: udvejayati lokāṃs trīn ucchritān dveṣṭi durmatiḥ śakraṃ tridaśarājānaṃ pradharṣayitum icchati
english: 'That evil-minded one harasses the three worlds, hates the exalted, and desires to overpower Śakra, the king of the thirty gods.'

sanskrit: ṛṣīn yakṣān sagandharvān asurān brāhmaṇāṃs tathā atikrāmati durdharṣo varadānena mohitaḥ
english: 'He transgresses against ṛṣis, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, and brāhmaṇas alike — that irresistible one, deluded by the power of the boon.'

sanskrit: nainaṃ sūryaḥ pratapati pārśve vāti na mārutaḥ calormimālī taṃ dṛṣṭvā samudro 'pi na kampate
english: 'The sun does not blaze upon him; the wind does not blow at his side; even the ocean, garlanded with tossing waves, does not tremble upon beholding him.'

sanskrit: tan manan no bhayaṃ tasmād rākṣasād ghoradarśanāt vadhārthaṃ tasya bhagavann upāyaṃ kartum arhasi
english: 'Therefore, great is our fear of that rākṣasa of terrible aspect; O blessed one, it is fitting that you devise the means for his destruction.'

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ suraiḥ sarvaiś cintayitvā tato 'bravīt hantāyaṃ vihitas tasya vadhopāyo durātmanaḥ
english: Thus addressed by all the gods, he reflected and then spoke: 'Indeed, the means of slaying that evil-souled one has already been ordained.'

sanskrit: tena gandharvayakṣāṇāṃ devadānavarakṣasām avadhyo 'smīti vāg uktā tathety uktaṃ ca tan mayā
english: 'By him the words were spoken: ‘I am not to be slain by gandharvas, yakṣas, gods, dānavas, or rākṣasas’ — and I assented to that request.'

sanskrit: nākīrtayad avajñānāt tad rakṣo mānuṣāṃs tadā tasmāt sa mānuṣād vadhyo mṛtur nānyo 'sya vidyate
english: 'That rākṣasa did not mention human beings, out of contempt; therefore he is to be slain by a human being — there is no other death for him.'

sanskrit: etac chrutvā priyaṃ vākyaṃ brahmaṇā samudāhṛtam devā maharṣayaḥ sarve prahṛṣṭās te 'bhavaṃs tadā
english: Having heard this welcome speech pronounced by Brahmā, all the gods and great ṛṣis were then greatly rejoiced.

sanskrit: etasminn antare viṣṇur upayāto mahādyutiḥ brahmaṇā ca samāgamya tatra tasthau samāhitaḥ
english: At that very moment Viṣṇu of great splendour arrived; meeting with Brahmā there, he stood in composed readiness.

sanskrit: tam abruvan surāḥ sarve samabhiṣṭūya saṃnatāḥ tvāṃ niyokṣyāmahe viṣṇo lokānāṃ hitakāmyayā
english: All the gods, honouring him and bowing low, addressed him: 'O Viṣṇu, we shall appoint you for the welfare of the worlds.'

sanskrit: rājño daśarathasya tvam ayodhyādhipater vibho dharmajñasya vadānyasya maharṣisamatejasaḥ tasya bhāryāsu tisṛṣu hrīśrīkīrtyupamāsu ca viṣṇo putratvam āgaccha kṛtvātmānaṃ caturvidham
english: 'O mighty Viṣṇu, become the son of king Daśaratha, lord of Ayodhyā — he who is learned in dharma, bountiful, and equal in glory to the great ṛṣis. Divide yourself fourfold and take birth in his three wives, who are comparable to Modesty, Prosperity, and Fame.'

sanskrit: tatra tvaṃ mānuṣo bhūtvā pravṛddhaṃ lokakaṇṭakam avadhyaṃ daivatair viṣṇo samare jahi rāvaṇam
english: 'There, having assumed human form, O Viṣṇu, slay in battle Rāvaṇa — that thorn in the side of the worlds, grown mighty and invincible by the gods.'

sanskrit: sa hi devān sagandharvān siddhāṃś ca ṛṣisattamān rākṣaso rāvaṇo mūrkho vīryotsekena bādhate
english: 'For that rākṣasa, the foolish Rāvaṇa, oppresses the gods together with the gandharvas, the siddhas, and the foremost of ṛṣis through the arrogance of his might.'

sanskrit: tad uddhataṃ rāvaṇam ṛddhatejasaṃ pravṛddhadarpaṃ tridaśeśvaradviṣam virāvaṇaṃ sādhu tapasvikaṇṭakaṃ tapasvinām uddhara taṃ bhayāvaham
english: 'Therefore, deliver us from that haughty Rāvaṇa, blazing with splendour, swollen with pride, hostile to the lord of the thirty gods, ever-shrieking, truly a thorn to the ascetics — that fearsome one.'

sanskrit: tato nārāyaṇo viṣṇur niyuktaḥ surasattamaiḥ jānann api surān evaṃ ślakṣṇaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Then Nārāyaṇa Viṣṇu, having been appointed by the foremost of gods, knowing it all already, spoke these gentle words to the gods.

sanskrit: upāyaḥ ko vadhe tasya rākṣasādhipateḥ surāḥ yam ahaṃ taṃ samāsthāya nihanyām ṛṣikaṇṭakam
english: 'What means shall I employ for the slaying of that lord of rākṣasas, O gods, adopting which I might kill that thorn-in-the-side-of-the-ṛṣis?'

sanskrit: evam uktāḥ surāḥ sarve pratyūcur viṣṇum avyayam mānuṣīṃ tanum āsthāya rāvaṇaṃ jahi saṃyuge
english: Thus addressed, all the gods replied to the imperishable Viṣṇu: 'Assuming a human body, slay Rāvaṇa in battle.'

sanskrit: sa hi tepe tapas tīvraṃ dīrghakālam ariṃdama yena tuṣṭo 'bhavad brahmā lokakṛl lokapūjitaḥ
english: 'For he practised fierce austerities for a long time, O subduer of enemies, by which Brahmā — maker of worlds, worshipped by the worlds — was pleased.'

sanskrit: saṃtuṣṭaḥ pradadau tasmai rākṣasāya varaṃ prabhuḥ nānāvidhebhyo bhūtebhyo bhayaṃ nānyatra mānuṣāt
english: 'Being well pleased, the lord bestowed a boon upon that rākṣasa: freedom from fear from all manner of beings, excepting only human beings.'

sanskrit: avajñātāḥ purā tena varadānena mānavāḥ tasmāt tasya vadho dṛṣṭo mānuṣebhyaḥ paraṃtapa
english: 'Human beings were despised by him of old on account of that boon; therefore his death at the hands of men has been foreseen, O scorcher of foes.'

sanskrit: ity etad vacanaṃ śrutvā surāṇāṃ viṣṇur ātmavān pitaraṃ rocayām āsa tadā daśarathaṃ nṛpam
english: Having heard these words of the gods, the self-possessed Viṣṇu then chose Daśaratha as the father into whom he would take birth.

sanskrit: sa cāpy aputro nṛpatis tasmin kāle mahādyutiḥ ayajat putriyām iṣṭiṃ putrepsur arisūdanaḥ
english: And that king of great splendour, who was himself without a son at that time, was performing the putrīyā iṣṭi, longing for sons, he the slayer of enemies.

sanskrit: tato vai yajamānasya pāvakād atulaprabham prādurbhūtaṃ mahad bhūtaṃ mahāvīryaṃ mahābalam
english: Then from the sacrificial fire of the sacrificer there emerged a great being of incomparable radiance, of mighty power and great strength.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇaṃ raktāmbaradharaṃ raktāsyaṃ dundubhisvanam snigdhaharyakṣatanujaśmaśrupravaramūrdhajam
english: Dark of complexion, clad in red garments, red-faced, with a voice like a kettledrum, with smooth tawny eyes, a body like a lion, and the finest beard and hair —

sanskrit: śubhalakṣaṇasaṃpannaṃ divyābharaṇabhūṣitam śailaśṛṅgasamutsedhaṃ dṛptaśārdūlavikramam
english: — possessed of auspicious marks, adorned with divine ornaments, of stature equal to a mountain peak, with the gait of a proud tiger —

sanskrit: divākarasamākāraṃ dīptānalaśikhopamam taptajāmbūnadamayīṃ rājatāntaparicchadām
english: — of appearance like the sun, comparable to a blazing flame, bearing a vessel of refined jāmbūnada gold with a silver lid —

sanskrit: divyapāyasasaṃpūrṇāṃ pātrīṃ patnīm iva priyām pragṛhya vipulāṃ dorbhyāṃ svayaṃ māyāmayīm iva
english: — holding in both vast arms that bowl filled with divine pāyasa (rice-milk), like a beloved wife, or as if it were made of illusion itself —

sanskrit: samavekṣyābravīd vākyam idaṃ daśarathaṃ nṛpam prājāpatyaṃ naraṃ viddhi mām ihābhyāgataṃ nṛpa
english: — he gazed upon king Daśaratha and spoke these words: 'Know me, O king, as a man sent by Prajāpati, who has come hither.'

sanskrit: tataḥ paraṃ tadā rājā pratyuvāca kṛtāñjaliḥ bhagavan svāgataṃ te 'stu kim ahaṃ karavāṇi te
english: Thereupon the king replied with joined palms: 'O blessed one, be welcome. What may I do for you?'

sanskrit: atho punar idaṃ vākyaṃ prājāpatyo naro 'bravīt rājann arcayatā devān adya prāptam idaṃ tvayā
english: Then that man sent by Prajāpati spoke again: 'O king, this has been obtained by you today through your worship of the gods.'

sanskrit: idaṃ tu naraśārdūla pāyasaṃ devanirmitam prajākaraṃ gṛhāṇa tvaṃ dhanyam ārogyavardhanam
english: 'This pāyasa has been made by the gods, O tiger among men — it is the source of progeny; take it, it is auspicious and enhances health.'

sanskrit: bhāryāṇām anurūpāṇām aśnīteti prayaccha vai tāsu tvaṃ lapsyase putrān yadarthaṃ yajase nṛpa
english: 'Give it to your worthy wives to eat; from them you shall obtain the sons for whose sake you are sacrificing, O king.'

sanskrit: tatheti nṛpatiḥ prītaḥ śirasā pratigṛhya tām pātrīṃ devānnasaṃpūrṇāṃ devadattāṃ hiraṇmayīm
english: Saying 'So be it,' the king, filled with joy, received upon his head that golden vessel filled with divine food, given by the gods.

sanskrit: abhivādya ca tad bhūtam adbhutaṃ priyadarśanam mudā paramayā yuktaś cakārābhipradakṣiṇam
english: He paid obeisance to that wondrous, fair-featured being, and filled with supreme joy, circumambulated him with reverence.

sanskrit: tato daśarathaḥ prāpya pāyasaṃ devanirmitam babhūva paramaprītaḥ prāpya vittam ivādhanaḥ
english: Then Daśaratha, having obtained the god-made pāyasa, was supremely delighted — like a penniless man who has received wealth.

sanskrit: tatas tad adbhutaprakhyaṃ bhūtaṃ paramabhāsvaram saṃvartayitvā tat karma tatraivāntaradhīyata
english: Then that wondrous and supremely resplendent being, having concluded that act, vanished on the spot.

sanskrit: harṣaraśmibhir udyotaṃ tasyāntaḥpuram ābabhau śāradasyābhirāmasya candrasyeva nabho'ṃśubhiḥ
english: His inner palace shone ablaze with rays of joy, as the sky shines with the beams of the delightful autumnal moon.

sanskrit: so 'ntaḥpuraṃ praviśyaiva kausalyām idam abravīt pāyasaṃ pratigṛhṇīṣva putrīyaṃ tv idam ātmanaḥ
english: Entering the inner apartments, he said to Kausalyā: 'Receive this pāyasa, which shall give you a son.'

sanskrit: kausalyāyai narapatiḥ pāyasārdhaṃ dadau tadā ardhād ardhaṃ dadau cāpi sumitrāyai narādhipaḥ kaikeyyai cāvaśiṣṭārdhaṃ dadau putrārthakāraṇāt
english: The lord of men gave half the pāyasa to Kausalyā; of the remaining half he gave half to Sumitrā; the remaining quarter he gave to Kaikeyī, for the purpose of obtaining sons.

sanskrit: pradadau cāvaśiṣṭārdhaṃ pāyasasyāmṛtopamam anucintya sumitrāyai punar eva mahīpatiḥ
english: And the remaining portion of that pāyasa, comparable to nectar, the lord of the earth gave again to Sumitrā after reflection.

sanskrit: evaṃ tāsāṃ dadau rājā bhāryāṇāṃ pāyasaṃ pṛthak
english: In this manner the king distributed the pāyasa separately to each of his wives.

sanskrit: tās tv etat pāyasaṃ prāpya narendrasyottamāḥ striyaḥ saṃmānaṃ menire sarvāḥ praharṣoditacetasaḥ
english: Those most excellent wives of the lord of men, having received this pāyasa, all considered themselves honoured, their hearts uplifted with exceeding joy.
